svg.title: Blind ring: NHL '94 and NHL '95
svg.text: Through the legs: NHL '94's blind ring and NHL '95's (Genesis)
Seen from above, to scale. Each goalie faces down the page; his net is above him. Where a low puck gets no stick and no body test, it slides through him.
NHL '94: butterfly (frame 480)
the ring round the blade
NHL '95: left stick save (frame 634)
measured, one frame each spot
NHL '95: standing (ready, frame 610)
measured, one frame each spot
A round ring, 8-14 from the blade:
the blade is 9 to his side, so the ring
covers his middle: a fast low puck steps
over the sliver of body in front.
A square box (the address bug): the blade
is 10 to his side, and the box reaches
his middle: a channel straight through him.
Standing, his body is never tested: his
reach, 14, lies inside the ±14 box, so only
the blade's 8 plays the puck.
body reach: NHL '94 13 here (12-15 by Agility); NHL '95 18 in this save (14-19); dashed: never tested
within 8 of the blade (white ring) the stick plays a low puck
nothing is tested: NHL '94 a ring 8-14 from the blade; NHL '95 a square ±14 round it, less the 8
NHL '95, measured: a slow low puck put there passed untouched (inside his reach)
Red: the goal line. Under the shapes, each game's own picture of that frame (NHL '94 frame 480; NHL '95 634 and 610). NHL '95's dots: a slow puck at height 0 put at each spot 2 units apart,
one frame played (gen95_blind_ring_check.py). In both games only a puck at height 5 or less meets the stick test; NHL '95's other frames (gloves, skating) have holes too, its dive none.
